accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England, Year 5 measurement ('estimate volume [for example, using 1 cm³ blocks to build cuboids (including cubes)] and capacity [for example, using water]') and Year 6 volume statements, and Common Core 5.MD.C.3–4 (unit cubes packed without gaps or overlaps; count unit cubes in cubic cm). Every number recomputed: 3 × 2 × 2 = 6 × 2 × 1 = 12; 5 × 4 = 20 a layer, × 3 = 60; 9.8 × 5.1 × 4.2 = 209.916, rounded edges 10 × 5 × 4 = 200; 9.9 × 4.1 × 2.8 = 113.7, estimate 10 × 4 × 3 = 120; 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre and 1 cm³ = 1 ml (SI definition of the litre as 1 dm³). Benchmarks: standard 16 mm dice ≈ 4.1 cm³; household matchbox about 5.3 × 3.6 × 1.5 cm ≈ 29 cm³ ('about 25'); large hen's egg about 55–60 ml; a mug about 250–350 ml; a medium apple about 200 cm³; a shoebox about 30 × 20 × 12 cm ≈ 7,200 cm³; a size 5 football (circumference 68–70 cm, diameter about 22 cm) ≈ 5,600 cm³. Each falls inside the band it is sorted into. Parameterised answers (a*b, l*10, l*w*2, n) were checked at the corners of their ranges by gate_items.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the volume errors documented by Battista and Clements (1996, 'Students' understanding of three-dimensional rectangular arrays of cubes'), the Common Core Geometric Measurement progression and NCETM Year 5/6 measurement guidance: judging volume by one dimension (step 1 prediction 'A, it is taller' / 'B, it is longer', challenge tag look, m1), adding edge lengths (prediction '12', rounding choice 19, tags add, p1), counting only one layer (prediction '20', rounding choice 50, tag layer, m8), unit confusion cm and cm² (tags unit, sq, m3), wildly-off estimates with no benchmark (step 3 sort with a specific reason per object, tags tiny and huge), and the litre–cm³ link (prediction '100 ml', tags hund and ten). Partial-jug capacity estimates are covered by tags round and drop and m6.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 565 Capacity and volume (flagcups) fills containers with cups; 855 Volume as additive (flagvadd) splits L-shaped solids; 892 scale factors. This lab is about estimating volume with 1 cm³ cubes: building two 12-cube blocks of different shape row by row, filling a 5 × 4 × 3 box one row then one layer at a time, sorting eight real objects against cube/matchbox/litre benchmarks, rounding a box's decimal edges before estimating, and filling a 10 cm cube to pour exactly 1 litre.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text states it: the two block counters both reach 12 although one is twice as long; in the box task 'Stack a layer' is refused until the first layer is filled, and the readout jumps 20 → 40 → 60; each wrong sort gives the object's real size in cubes; the rounding task refuses 98 and 19 with the reason and the canvas relabels the box 10 cm, 5 cm, 4 cm; pouring is refused until all 10 layers are in, and the 1,000 cm³ of water fills the jug exactly to the 1 litre line.

predictions.evidence: Step 1: 'Which has the bigger volume?' with 'A, it is taller' and 'B, it is longer' tempting; both blocks reach 12 cubes. Step 2: '5 × 4 × 3 box: 12, 20 or 60 cubes?' with 12 (adding edges) and 20 (one layer) tempting; the stacked box shows 60. Step 5: '10 cm cube of water: 30 ml, 100 ml or 1 litre?' with 30 (adding) and 100 (one layer) tempting; pouring shows 1 litre.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each distractor in the eight challenge questions has its own tag and WHY message in estvol_art.js (add, layer, tiny, huge, look, hund, ten, round, drop, unit, sq). In the lab, every wrong object bin, every wrong rounding choice (9, 98, 6, 51, 5, 42, 19, 50), overfilling a block or box, stacking before a layer is complete and pouring an unfilled box each give a message naming that slip.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability check passes (learner kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5). Kid sentences are short ('Count the cubes.'), and the precise Year 5 terms (volume, cubic centimetre, cm³, cuboid, layer, estimate, capacity, litre, ml) are used and explained where they first appear.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs match the cube, layer, benchmark/rounding and litre ideas; the adult text gives the curriculum statement, exactly what each task does with its numbers, and the named mistakes; every hint names a step to take (count one layer, round to 10, 5 and 4, compare with a matchbox).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots of every step at start and after Show me at 360 px (Android, 2x) in light theme and checked by eye. The first pass clipped block B at the right edge at 360 px; cube size is now computed from the canvas width so both blocks fit with a gap, and the litre box now empties when poured. Bins are a 2 × 2 grid of 46 px tap targets; every action also has a full-width button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Add a row to A/B, Fill a row of 5, Stack a layer, the four bins, the rounding choices, Add a layer of 100 cm³, Pour into the jug), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the cube count, layers, sorted object, rounded edges or water poured.
